EOMasters Newsletter #034

27/10/2024

Hello EO-Masters!

In this issue I let you how you can probably process your data faster, tell you more about the latest SNAP release, tell you where you can meet me and some more interesting news.

Now, let's head over to the news.

EOMasters News

GPF Runner - Process Your Data Faster

This little project aims to help you to run processing with ESA SNAP faster. In some cases, the gpt tool does not execute with the best possible performance. GPF Runner can be more than 5-times faster than a normal GPF run.

Sure, it needs a bit of Java development, but I tried to make it as easy as possible and there are also some examples.

If you have questions, don't hesitate to ask me in the EOMasters forum.

  • GpfRunner on GitHub

EO and RS News

LPS Calls for Abstracts

Credits: ESA

You probably already heard that ESA's Living Planet Symposium takes place next year in Vienna between 23-27 June. You might also have heard that the abstract submission is open. However, it should not be missing from an EO newsletter.

The theme for this year is "From Observation to Climate Action and Sustainability for Earth"

You can send your abstract till 1 December 2024.

In addition, you can also preregister as a sponsor for the event. Being a sponsor ensures that you are seen by the EO community.

  • LPS Abstract Submission

  • Call for Sponsors - Preregistration

2nd EO Commercialisation Forum

Credit: ESA

The second EO Commercialisation Forum takes place in Frankfurt in November. There are several good reasons to visit this forum.

  • Networking Opportunities

  • Market Insights

  • Investment Opportunities

  • Keynote Speakers

  • Awards and Recognition

And the best is, you can meet me. Drop me a line if you want to meet.

  • ESA’s Earth Observation Commercialisation Forum

Draco - A Satellite to Be Destroyed

Credit: ESA/D. Ducros

The Draco mission (Destructive Re-entry Assessment Container Object) aims to ensure that satellites burn up completely on re-entry. The sequence of events during the destructive re-entry of a satellite is to be recorded with the Draco mission. This shall help to reduce existing uncertainties in demolition and dismantling processes.

The mission is planned for 2027 and will involve a 150-kilogram satellite.

  • Draco mission made for destruction

New Release of ESA's SNAP

The development team of ESA's SNAP has released version 11 last week. I provide an overview of the changes beyond the official changelog. It also includes the API changes and points out some issues you might experience, including viable solutions.

  • EOMasters Blog: SNAP 11 - What's new?

That's it for this issue. I hope you enjoyed this collection of news. Stay tuned for the next edition, which will arrive in your inbox in about two weeks.

Tschüss and Goodbye!

Marco
